mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is above 2% annualized, the market anticipates aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, the market anticipates a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or the interaction of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in GDP (GDPC1) growth rate below 2% annualized signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or GDPC1 growth < 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.
